mechanism_narrative: The EGFR+LIFR forced-proximity novokine (flexible_GS4 linker, ~20 Å) biases signaling by enabling EGFR's intrinsic tyrosine kinase to transphosphorylate LIFR's ICD, while LIFR-associated JAK1/JAK2 reciprocally phosphorylate EGFR. This synergistic cross-talk activates three axes: (1) GRB2/SHC1→RAS→MAPK/ERK via EGFR pY1068/pY1086 and LIFR/JAK phosphotyrosines; (2) GAB1/PIK3R1→PI3K→AKT via EGFR pY845/pY1173 and LIFR/JAK-recruited adaptors; and (3) JAK1/JAK2→STAT3 via LIFR box1/JAK interaction. PLCG1 is sterically excluded because the short GS4 linker (~20 Å) cannot span the asymmetric ECD geometry (EGFR ~621 aa vs LIFR ~789 aa ECD) to position PLCG1's SH2 domains for productive docking at both EGFR pY992 and LIFR/JAK phosphosites simultaneously. The biased output (MAPK↑, AKT↑, STAT3↑, PLCγ↓) promotes muscle structural gene expression and satellite cell self-renewal while suppressing aged IEGs and inflammatory markers.
